title: Exact fractions
text: fractions can’t stored exactly number, arithmetic approximate. number also forgets written: 3 10 30 100 0.3. rhind package stores numerator n denominator d separately, keeps exact value terms written .
code: 1 / 10 + 2 / 10 == 3 / 10 #> [1] FALSE  fraction(1, 10) + fraction(2, 10) == fraction(3, 10) #> [1] TRUE

title: Exact fractions
text: fraction vctrs record two fields. works like vector, including data frames. denominator zero allowed: 1/0, -1/0 0/0 behave Inf, -Inf NaN.
code: x <- fraction(c(2, 1, -5, NA), c(4, 3, 1, 1)) x #> <fraction<double>[4]> #> [1] 2/4 1/3  -5  NA numerator(x) #> [1]  2  1 -5 NA denominator(x) #> [1]  4  3  1 NA

title: Exact fractions
text: as_fraction() reads text, approximates numbers aren’t whole.
code: as_fraction(c("2/4", "3", "1 3/4")) #> <fraction<integer>[3]> #> [1] 2/4   3 7/4 as_fraction(c(0.1, 0.75, 1 / 3)) #> <fraction<double>[3]> #> [1] 1/10  3/4  1/3 as_fraction(pi, max_d = 1000) #> <fraction<double>[1]> #> [1] 355/113 as.double(fraction(1, 3)) #> [1] 0.3333333

title: Exact fractions
text: Fractions kept written, results lowest terms. simplify() reduces fraction without calculating anything. Functions results usually aren’t fractions, sqrt() exp(), give doubles.
code: fraction(1, 3) + fraction(1, 6) #> <fraction<double>[1]> #> [1] 1/2 fraction(2, 3)^-2 #> <fraction<double>[1]> #> [1] 9/4 simplify(fraction(2, 4)) #> <fraction<double>[1]> #> [1] 1/2 sum(fraction(1, 1:10)) #> <fraction<double>[1]> #> [1] 7381/2520 mean(fraction(1:3, 4)) #> <fraction<double>[1]> #> [1] 1/2 round(fraction(2, 3), 2) #> <fraction<double>[1]> #> [1] 67/100

title: Exact fractions
text: Whole numbers fractions. element plain number isn’t whole, result double, adding integer double. Convert as_fraction() first remain exact. type made combining vectors can’t depend values, combining double gives doubles. Use integers (1L) as_fraction() combine fractions.
code: fraction(1, 3) + 1 #> <fraction<double>[1]> #> [1] 4/3 fraction(1, 3) + 0.5 #> [1] 0.8333333 fraction(1, 3) + as_fraction(0.5) #> <fraction<double>[1]> #> [1] 5/6 c(fraction(1, 3), 1) #> [1] 0.3333333 1.0000000 c(fraction(1, 3), 1L) #> <fraction<double>[2]> #> [1] 1/3   1

title: Exact fractions
text: Comparisons use exact value, regardless terms. sorting, matching grouping.
code: fraction(2, 4) == fraction(1, 2) #> [1] TRUE unique(fraction(c(2, 1, 1), c(4, 2, 3))) #> <fraction<double>[2]> #> [1] 2/4 1/3 sort(fraction(c(2, 1, 5), c(3, 2, 8))) #> <fraction<double>[3]> #> [1] 1/2 5/8 2/3

title: Exact fractions

title: Arithmetic with fractions — fraction-arithmetic
text: Results exact, lowest terms. Whole numbers fractions, results ordinary doubles element plain number whole, usually exact. Use as_fraction() convert first.

title: Arithmetic with fractions — fraction-arithmetic
text: Arithmetic +, -, *, /, %% %/% exact. ^ exact exponents whole numbers, otherwise gives doubles. Inputs must size, size 1. Summaries sum(), prod(), mean(), median(), min(), max() range() exact. quantile() gives doubles. Cumulative cumsum(), cumprod(), cummin() cummax() exact. Rounding round(), floor(), ceiling() trunc() exact. round() gives even digit halves. signif() gives doubles. functions abs() sign() give fractions. exp(), log(), sqrt() give doubles. result needs numbers large integers, results stored doubles. Results need numbers larger 2^53 missing, warning. Use .double() calculate approximately instead. Logical operators (&, |, !, (), ()) supported. Base R finds methods functions like sum() first argument, use sum(x, 1) instead sum(1, x).

code: fraction(1, 3) + fraction(1, 6) #> <fraction<double>[1]> #> [1] 1/2 fraction(2, 3) * 2 #> <fraction<double>[1]> #> [1] 4/3 fraction(2, 3)^-2 #> <fraction<double>[1]> #> [1] 9/4  # Not all whole numbers fraction(1, 2) + 0.25 #> [1] 0.75 fraction(1, 2) + as_fraction(0.25) #> <fraction<double>[1]> #> [1] 3/4  sum(fraction(1, 1:10)) #> <fraction<double>[1]> #> [1] 7381/2520 cumsum(fraction(1, c(2, 4, 8))) #> <fraction<double>[3]> #> [1] 1/2 3/4 7/8
